https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.speaker: Lisa D. Cook
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.title: The U.S. Economy in Global Context
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.label: Hawkish · supports further tightening
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.evidence: I am skeptical that September's single 1/4 point rate increase will be enough to change the path of inflation.
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.rationale: Cook judged financial conditions too accommodative and said waiting carried inflation risks. She had preferred another quarter-point increase in October. The size and number of future moves still depended on the data.

priorOutlook.label: 28 September policy outlook
priorOutlook.comparison: Cook’s September outlook left the direction of her next preferred move open and tied its size and timing to inflation, labour data and the effects of past actions. On 20 November she argued that one increase was unlikely to be enough. This establishes a newly explicit tightening preference. September supplies no numerical starting score, so subtracting zero from November’s +2 would overstate what can be measured.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.speaker: Christopher J. Waller
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.title: Opening Remarks at the 2026 College Fed Challenge Finals
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.label: No rate guidance · student competition
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.evidence: The challenge is to prepare and present a monetary policy recommendation
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.rationale: Waller described the decision students would present at the College Fed Challenge. The assignment expresses no personal preference for the next policy decision.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.title: Monetary Policy amid Frequent and Complex Shocks
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.label: Two-sided conditions · no preferred direction
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.evidence: If price pressures are contained, it may be prudent to prioritize downside risks to employment.
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.rationale: Jefferson would respond more strongly to inflation if expectations risked becoming unanchored. Contained price pressure would give more weight to employment. He did not choose between the scenarios or advocate holding rates.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.speaker: Michael S. Barr
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.title: Investing in America’s Underserved Communities
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.label: Hawkish lean · conditional on his forecast
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.evidence: If the economy evolves as I currently forecast, I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.rationale: In a speech mainly about community investment, Barr included a personal policy outlook. His forecast points to further increases, with timing and size left open.

priorOutlook.label: 29 September policy outlook
priorOutlook.comparison: In his September outlook Barr expected further policy adjustments in his base case after a rate increase, citing greater inflation risks and receding labour-market risks. He did not specify the direction of those adjustments in that passage. November explicitly names further increases under his forecast. The wording is clearer, but it does not establish that he wanted a larger hike. His 16 November financial-stability speech offered no comparable rate outlook.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.speaker: Christopher J. Waller
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.title: Considerations at the Intersection of Payments and Tokenized Markets
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.label: No rate guidance · payment systems
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.evidence: The Federal Reserve can support these solutions by providing core payment and settlement infrastructure upon which the private sector can innovate
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.rationale: Waller discussed how settlement infrastructure and tokenization could affect payments. He did not give a current preference for the federal funds rate.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.speaker: Kevin Warsh
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.title: Opening Remarks at the Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.label: No rate guidance · productivity research
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.evidence: Will this new technology deliver a rise in total factor productivity?
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.rationale: Warsh described possible productivity and employment outcomes and their longer-run implications for monetary policy. The remarks did not specify a preferred current rate path.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.speaker: Michael S. Barr
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.title: Some Potential Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.label: No rate guidance · financial stability
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.evidence: In addition to the question of equity valuations, the AI buildout has been increasingly funded by debt.
https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevent.rationale: Barr examined leverage in data centers and vulnerabilities linked to AI adoption. The risks he discussed concern financial stability and carry no explicit recommendation for the policy rate.
